note: The tags an idea map uses (EE-059): Naive's own conventions, never free-form labels. Each idea in a founder's idea dump is tagged with the departments it bears on (operations/departments.json, APQC with Porter's value chain), the records it feeds (schema/data-model.json), and whether it describes something that already exists. Its pillar follows from its first department. Each idea keeps at most max.departments departments and max.records records, strongest first, at or above the threshold. Version 0.x, ours and unevaluated.

departments.strategy: the venture's direction, vision, positioning against competitors, or what to do first
departments.products: designing, building or improving a product, feature or service the venture offers
departments.marketing-and-sales: reaching, persuading or selling to customers: channels, content, campaigns, launches, sales
departments.supply-chain: sourcing, making or moving physical goods
departments.service-delivery: delivering a service to customers day to day
departments.customer-service: supporting, onboarding or keeping customers after they buy
departments.human-capital: people: cofounders, hiring, roles, culture, the founder's own development
departments.it: the technology, data, infrastructure, integrations or AI the venture runs on
departments.finance: money: pricing, revenue, costs, funding, investors
departments.assets: property, equipment or other assets the venture buys or owns
departments.risk-and-compliance: legal, regulatory, privacy, security or other risks
departments.external-relationships: partners, community, investors relations, the public or government
departments.capabilities: how the venture improves itself: processes, knowledge, quality, measurement

validation-problem.about: a problem or pain that people have

icp.about: who the customer, user or audience is

product.about: a specific product, feature or offering

venture-core.about: the venture's core promise, who it is promised to, or the competence that makes it deliverable

telos.about: the long-run vision, end state, ambition or exit

validation-solution.about: how a problem would be solved

validation-go-to-market.about: how the venture would reach and win its first customers

validation-pricing.about: a price, a business model or how the venture makes money

validation-team.about: who would build or run the venture

alignment.about: principles, values, or what the venture must never do

brand.about: the venture's name, tagline, story or look

exists: the founder (or their team) has already built, launched or sold this product, prototype or pilot themselves; a competitor's product does not count
